messages:
inc-bot: Pager alert: elevated 5xx rate on Dedicated cluster d-phi-04 serving tenant zephyrlabs. 5xx spike started ~3m ago, gateway timeouts and KV evictions observed. Pager: https://pager.redwood/incident/3776543210 :rotating_light:

jordan (oncall): acked — joining. pulling graphs now.

megan (SRE): I'm on it. initial check: cluster d-phi-04 shows 5xx ~28% on ingress gateways, p95 latency jumped to ~2.4s. KV eviction rate on node group phi-hot is off the charts.

charu (eng-runtime): thanks. that sounds like a noisy-tenant eviction storm. is zephyrlabs the only tenant showing high QPS?

jordan (oncall): zephyrlabs QPS up ~6x last 10m relative to baseline. other tenants on the same pool show increased tail latencies but not the same QPS.

leon (infra): checking GPU / memory pressure on nodes. `kubectl top pods -n dedicated-d-phi-04 | sort -r -k3 | head` shows several pods at 98% memory and KV cache pressure on nodes phi-04-{02,05}.

megan (SRE): mitigation plan: 1) apply per-tenant request-rate cap for zephyrlabs at edge 2) enable routing of overflow to alternate pool d-phi-06 with spare capacity 3) temporarily increase cache eviction threshold to reduce thrashing 4) contact CSM/support to alert customer. doing them in that order.

charu (eng-runtime): for (3) we can flip the kv eviction window to 120s and bump allowed-kv-misses to 500 temporarily. command:```
# runtimectl on d-phi-04
runtimectl set --cluster d-phi-04 --kv-eviction-window=120s --kv-miss-threshold=500
```

leon (infra): prefunding d-phi-06 for overflow: `orch scale pool d-phi-06 --add 8-gpu --priority=emergency` — will take ~90s to spin new workers.

jordan (oncall): I'll push the tenant throttle at edge: `edgectl throttle tenant zephyrlabs --rps 1500 --burst 300`. applying now.

megan (SRE): applied throttle. within 30s 5xx dropped from 28% -> 12%. continuing.

sara (support): pinging Zephyr labs CSM / AM to give heads-up. message drafted: "We're seeing elevated errors from your traffic on a shared cluster, we've throttled to protect stability and routing some traffic to spare capacity. We'll coordinate a durable fix shortly." sending.

megan (SRE): runtime config updated (kv eviction window/threshold). node-level cache thrash reduced. post-change metrics: eviction rate down 85%.

charu (eng-runtime): pushed fallback routing rule: any request hitting gateway error will be routed to model-variant v1-fallback-hosted which is compatible and in d-phi-06. rule: `routingpolicy add -if 5xx>5% -> route to d-phi-06/v1-fallback-hosted`

leon (infra): d-phi-06 workers up and joined LB. verifying RB metrics: new pool capacity 8 GPUs, available slots increased by 60%.

jordan (oncall): after routing + throttle combined 5xx now ~3%, p95 latency down to 420ms. monitoring for 10m.

megan (SRE): checking logs from an affected request flow:```
ERROR gateway: upstream read timeout
stack: runtime/kv.go:421 evict: eviction triggered for tenant zephyrlabs
request_id=fx-9a7b
latency=2.6s
```

charu (eng-runtime): related note: model-runner for zephyrlabs is using long sequences and heavy KV reuse; with the noisy spike their KV working set exceeds per-node cache and causes expensive redis fallbacks. that's the thrash. longer-term we should recommend model quantization + pinned cache or dedicated pool for them.

megan (SRE): short-term mitigations done. next step: increase tenant isolation for zephyrlabs — propose a reserved subpool in d-phi-04 with 2 GPUs while they investigate unusual traffic pattern. leon/infra, can you spin a reserved subpool?

leon (infra): creating reservation: `orch reserve --cluster d-phi-04 --tenant zephyrlabs --gpus 2 --duration 24h --isolation=soft` — reserving now. ETA ~45s.

sara (support): Zephyr labs replied: they see a spike in a batch job that misfired and are disabling it. they asked for logs and RPS numbers. sharing dashboard and recent logs now.

jordan (oncall): confirming: reservation created and applied. traffic for zephyrlabs now largely on reserved subpool + overflow to d-phi-06. 5xx stabilized ~1.8%.

megan (SRE): handing over to oncall for monitoring window. I'll prepare an incident summary and RCA starter.

charu (eng-runtime): note for RCA: root cause = tenant-triggered workload spike causing KV working set pressure -> cache thrash -> upstream timeouts -> gateway 5xx spike. Mitigations: edge throttle, runtime kv window bump, routing to spillover pool, temporary reservation. Follow-ups: recommend dedicated pool for heavy batch jobs, or enforce per-tenant burst caps, add bulk-job detector.

leon (infra): infra action items: add automated cold-cache alarm when kv-eviction-rate > 50/s and downstream error rate > 5% for >1m. handle autoscale faster for dedicated pools.

sara (support): documenting customer impact: Zephyr labs: ~6m of elevated failures, ~2% of requests failed end-to-end despite mitigation before TTL, alerted customer and collected logs.

jordan (oncall): monitoring period complete (10m). metrics steady. I'm staying on until 22:30 UTC for final checks. handover to night oncall: @megan, @charu please post any additional notes you'll want included in the incident ticket.

megan (SRE): will add notes: exact commands, config delta, timeline, and recommend follow-ups — will also include suggested customer-specific pricing/ops path for dedicated reservation if they want permanent.

charu (eng-runtime): adding the runtime diffs: `kv-eviction-window: 60s -> 120s`, `kv-miss-threshold: 100 -> 500`, routing rule added, tenant throttle applied. revert plan: revert kv settings to baseline after 24h if stable; keep reservation until customer confirms traffic reduction.

inc-bot: Incident 3776543210 status: mitigated -> being monitored. Severity: S2. assigned owners: megan (SRE), jordan (oncall).

sara (support): I'll follow up with Zephyr labs and schedule a 1:1 to review batch-job patterns and offer a reserved pool option.

megan (SRE): thanks everyone. final note: no customer data exposure; changes were config/traffic-routing only. closing chat; will file a post-incident doc with RCA and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
